en: Laws of renouncing domain. Contains 4 paragraphs: One of the courtyard residents who forgot and did not make an eruv with the others restricts them. What is their remedy? He renounces his domain to them by saying "my domain is renounced to you" or "transferred to you," and no formal acquisition is required. He may renounce even after nightfall. If he lives with four or five others he must renounce to each one individually, saying "my domain is renounced to you and to you." Some say it suffices to say "my domain is renounced to all of you." If he renounced his domain without specification, he has only renounced his share in the courtyard — therefore they are permitted to carry from their houses to the courtyard, and he too is like a mere guest. But they are forbidden to carry from his house to the courtyard, and so is he. Some say he must lock his house so that he not come to carry out in a forbidden manner, and he should only open it when he wishes to enter or exit, locking it immediately after.

he: לך עט״ז הר״מ ז׳ל פרק שני דעירובין ה״ב ועב״י ומ״מ ובר״מ שם לך לך ולך ג״פ בשלשה דרין יחד שי״ל רוב משא״כ א׳ לשנים לכ״ע י״ל די שיאמר לכולכם ובש״ע כתב לך ולך ב״פ ומיהו זה לשון הטור בד׳ וה׳ כו׳ כאילו אמר לך ולך כו׳. וי״ל כי המחבר סובר דהלכה כי״א כי הביא רק לשון הטור וכתב וי״א שאין מפורש רק בטור יע״ש אי״ה ארשום בכללים. ומ״ש בנוסח ר״ה י״ג כ״ל וי״מ כל או כולו והוא קיים הגירסא להר״מ ז״ל כמ״ש ג״פ לך ולך ולך שלא נפרש רובו ככולו. ודברים ראוים למי שאמרן. ודע אם עומדי׳ רק מקצת בני החצר ואמר הריני מבטל לכולם י״ל כ״ע מודים דלאו מבוטל רק למה שעומדי׳ שם עמ״מ שכתב אם היו עומדים כולם כו׳ לכולכם וי״ל בין כולם לכולכם:
en: To you — Taz, Rambam z"l chapter 2 of Eruvin halacha 2, and Beit Yosef and nevertheless and in Rambam there: to you, to you, and to you three times when three dwell together—it can be explained as a majority; not so one to two, for all agree it can be explained that he says to all of you; and in Shulchan Aruch he wrote to you and to you twice. However, this is the language of the Tur in seifim 4 and 5, etc., as if he said to you and to you, etc. And it can be explained that the Mechaber holds the halacha is like one opinion, for he brought only the language of the Tur and wrote: and one says it is not explicit except in the Tur—see there; I will record it in the general principles. And what he wrote in the Rosh version: all or all of it—and the version stands for Rambam z"l as he wrote three times to you and to you and to you, that we do not explain the majority as the whole. And words fitting for one who spoke them. And know: if only part of the members of the courtyard stand and he says "I renounce to all of you," it can be explained that all agree he is not renounced except to those standing there; nevertheless, since he wrote if all were standing, etc., to all of you—it can be explained whether between all or to all of you:

he: וי״א עט״ז ועמ״א ו׳ ואי״ה שם יבואר ולהלכה עא״ר אות ו׳ צידד שם לומר דאין מועיל שכירות מישראל יע״ש:
en: Hashem’s Word and Hashem’s Word, and Hashem’s Word, and Hashem’s Word, and Hashem’s Word, and Hashem’s Word, and Hashem’s Word: “I am not afraid of Hashem’s mercy.”

en: It is not a word of Hashem’s word, nor is it in Hashem’s Word. And he said, “No, no, no, no, no, no, no, no, no, no, no matter what I am doing.”
